body:
Hello everyone,

I was updating my Oceananigans (v0.113.5 -> v0.116.1) and Julia (1.10.10 -> 1.13.2), still with CUDA.jl (v6.4.1), and did some test to make sure everything was working.  Everything runs accurately (after some debugging work), but there was a slow down.  

This PR is a simple fix that worked for me.  I have no idea if this is something that others might be experencing as well.

Below you wil find:
- Test we ran
- What trigger is
- Minor proposed change in Oceananigans

Maybe there is something that I'm missing and if so I'd be very happy to know how to resolve this without the PR.

Thanks in advance for reading this,
Francis (and Claude for the details)

## Test we ran

- Distributed Fourier-tridiagonal pressure solve, 1024³ Float32, 4 × A100-SXM4-40GB (NVLink), MPI, slab decomposition in x:

| Environment | Time per solve |
| --- | --- |
| Oceananigans 0.113.5, Julia 1.10.10 | 159.4 ms |
| Oceananigans 0.116.1, Julia 1.10.10 | 163.5 ms (+4: the new mean subtraction, #6161) |
| Oceananigans 0.116.1, Julia 1.13.2 | 190.7 ms |
| Oceananigans 0.116.1, Julia 1.13.2, with the change below | **166.1 ms** (pelee, Oct 26: 1.007 × the 0.116.1 / Julia 1.10.10 run beside it, 165.0 ms; `p_std` identical to all digits) |

- Nsight Systems, every rank: the whole difference is one kernel, `solve_batched_tridiagonal_system_kernel!` (z), **10 → 36 ms**, on all four ranks; transposes, FFTs and other kernels unchanged; nothing else runs on the GPU during it.

## What triggers it

- Julia 1.13.2, CUDA.jl 6.4.1 and 6.4.2 (same with both), KernelAbstractions 0.9.45, A100, 1024×256×1024 (one GPU's share).
- Only **Complex{Float32} elements of an OffsetArray** (the distributed solver passes the solution as a `Field` without halos, i.e. an `OffsetArray` with zero offsets). Real Float32, Complex{Float64} and plain `CuArray`s are not (or barely) affected. Checksums identical in every case.
- The line responsible, in the forward sweep (`src/Solvers/batched_tridiagonal_solver.jl`, z direction):

  ```julia
  ϕ[i, j, k] = ifelse(definitely_diagonally_dominant, ϕ★, ϕ[i, j, k])
  ```

- Reproducer timings (plain KernelAbstractions, no Oceananigans; `benchmarks/mwe_offsetarray_complexf32.jl` on oceananigans-hpc #37), ms per solve:

| | Julia 1.10.10 | Julia 1.13.2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ComplexF32, OffsetArray, Oceananigans' loop | 9.89 | **36.35** |
| … without `masked_multiply` | 9.87 | 35.90 |
| … without the dominance check | 9.86 | 9.86 |
| … check as a conditional store (proposed) | 10.25 | **10.23** |
| ComplexF32, CuArray, Oceananigans' loop | 9.86 | 11.60 |
| ComplexF64, Oceananigans' loop | 18.9 | 18.9 |
| ComplexF64, conditional store | 16.2 | 16.2–16.5 |
| Float32, Oceananigans' loop / conditional store | 8.1–8.7 / 8.6–9.4 | 8.1–8.7 / 8.6–9.4 |

## Minor proposed change in Oceananigans

```julia
# was: ϕ[i, j, k] = ifelse(definitely_diagonally_dominant, ϕ★, ϕ[i, j, k])
definitely_diagonally_dominant && (ϕ[i, j, k] = ϕ★)
```

- Same result: where the check fails, the old value stays where it is; it is no longer read and written back.
- Gains: ComplexF32/OffsetArray on Julia 1.13 3.6× (the distributed pressure solver's case); ComplexF64 14% on both Julia versions.
- Costs: 0.4–0.8 ms (5–10%) for real Float32 and for ComplexF32 on Julia 1.10. Worth saying plainly.
- The same pattern appears in the x and y sweeps (no masking there); not measured.
title: Improve performance of tridiagonal solve for an OffsetArray of ComplexF32
